newsitem.title: USA: Cold weather still a threat to Mexican coffee belt.
newsitem.headline: Cold weather still a threat to Mexican coffee belt.

text.p: A cold airmass seen surging from Texas down into Mexico late Tuesday is expected to reach the country's coffee-growing regions by late Wednesday and could threaten the northern portion of the coffee belt, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said Tuesday.

Davis said in his daily update that the two coldest mornings will be Thursday and Friday, with low temperatures ranging from around 30 degrees (Farenheit) in the far northern section of the belt to around 40 degrees in the far southern section of the belt.

"Because coffee is grown in hilly terrain, there will be a wide variety of temperatures as readings drop off more in valleys and stay up a bit more on hilltops," Davis said. "These low temperatures late this week are a threat to the coffee crop in parts of the belt."
Davis said while it does not look as if the cold weather will bring widespread damage, there is a potential for some damage in some sections of the Mexican coffee belt.
"The primary threat right now looks like it will be to coffee in the northern portion of the belt," he said.
By late weekend and early next week, Davis said temperatures will moderate.
